done.why: The carousel room sent me to random exits, so I could not get back to the well with my teapot of water. The oddly-angled room puzzle gave me no rule I could work out. I had used many turns going in circles.

about: A Zork II style cave world. You collect treasures south of a ravine while a prankish Wizard casts spells on you. There are riddles and odd rooms: a carousel that scrambles exits, a lizard-guarded door, a well with a bucket, and a room that counts steps like a baseball diamond.

moments.note: The Wizard's arrival speech hints at the pearls, the stone door and the carousel. It works as a gentle guide.
Walking into the Carousel Room, the exits turned out to be scrambled.
I fed the clay brick to the lizard on impulse, and it was gone. I suspect I wasted something useful.
The oddly-angled rooms behaved randomly. 'Woken' and 'lost count' appeared without a pattern I could use.
I answered 'well' to the riddle and the stone door opened, which got me the pearl necklace.
Getting into the bucket and pouring made me lightheaded. Afterwards my movement was random for a while.
The carousel's random exits made returning to the well tedious across about 30 turns.

wished: A clue for how the carousel can be stopped or steered
A clearer indication of the base-running order in the oddly-angled rooms
To see what the dragon, the unicorn and the menhir did

lines.line: It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid, and much good may it do you; the pearls nearest, behind a stone door that asks a question
lines.why: The Wizard gives you the goal and a direction in character.

lines.line: A thing that is turned can presumably be stopped, by somebody who finds the works.
lines.why: A fair hint that the carousel can be solved.

lines.line: it goes dark when the count is lost, which it is by any step but the right one.
lines.why: This explains the window puzzle rule, but the exits were still too opaque for me to solve it.

fun.why: The riddle door and the pearls were satisfying. The random carousel and the opaque puzzle room wore me down.

engagement.why: The Wizard's mischief and the new puzzles kept me curious, but I stalled in loops.

difficulty.why: The step order in the oddly-angled rooms was unreadable, and the carousel gave me no way to steer.

interestingness.why: A varied set of locations, plus new twists on a known cave: illusions, the carousel, and a baseball diamond room.

prose.why: The extra narration around the Wizard and the odd rooms is witty and clear.
